subject: science
passage: Convergent evolution, the independent appearance of similar traits in lineages that are not closely related, has usually been documented in anatomy: the wings of bats and birds, for instance, or the streamlined bodies of sharks and dolphins. Researchers comparing genetic sequences have now identified a number of cases in which convergence extends to the level of individual molecules. ______ echolocating bats and toothed whales, two groups whose common ancestor could not echolocate, share several of the same amino acid changes in prestin, a protein in the inner ear involved in hearing high-frequency sounds.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The second sentence says researchers have found "a number of cases" of molecular convergence. The last sentence describes one such case: matching changes in prestin in bats and toothed whales. The transition must introduce one instance of a general claim about several cases.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Specifically" would present the bat and whale case as a more precise statement of the whole claim, but the claim covers "a number of cases," and this is only one of them. This is the most attractive near miss.
explanation.B: Correct. "For example" signals that the prestin case is one of the "number of cases" just mentioned.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals a contrast, but the prestin case supports the claim about molecular convergence.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The shared prestin changes are not a result of researchers comparing sequences; the comparison revealed them.
